To quote Violent J "We like cartoon serial slaughterers on our records. It's how we adjust to the pressures of life. When I was in high school I was pretty deep into it. I had an ICP hat, a hatchet man necklace, a bunch of shirts and even a psychopathic back pack. One day I'm called into the office and told that all of my hatchet gear is against the dress code and I'm not allowed to wear it. I was flabbergasted, as this had never once come up before. When I inquired why, they told me it's because the hatchet man symbol is a gang sign. That's how I became number 4 of the 5 most gang related individuals at my school. (Trust me, if you knew me, This would be fucking hilarious.) However sadly, other juggalos have tried to form gangs and shit. When I was visiting a large mall north from where I live. Because it's gang related, and just a few weeks before, there was a juggalo gang fight in which someone was thrown through a glass window. What in the actual fuck? ICP tells juggalos it's about unity and solidarity. Not fighting each other, or burning off "undeserved" tattoos. But I digress. Eventually I started falling away from it. Other fans I would meet more and more frequently were single minded, drug addled ignorant dumb asses. Slowly but surely I stopped saying hi to them on the streets as I drifted further away. Do I regret being a Juggalo? No, not at all. Because it taught me some important stuff like: Not everyone is going to like your music so don't force it on them, just enjoy it yourself. Don't give a fuck about what others thing, their opinion isn't worth your time. Don't be a dick to people. And finally, people will be a dick to you based on preconceived notions, that's life. Berbers live in groups scattered across NorthAfrica whose origins and genetic relationships with their neighbours are not well established. The first hypervariablesegment of the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) control region was sequenced in a total of 155 individuals from three Tunisian Berber groups and compared to other North Africans. The mtDNA lineages found belong to a common set of mtDNA haplogroups already described in NorthAfrica. Besides the autochthonous North African U6 haplogroup, a group of L3 lineages characterized by the transition at position 16041 seems to be restricted to North Africans, suggesting that an expansion of this group of lineages took place around 10500 years ago in NorthAfrica, and spread to neighbouring populations. Principal components and the coordinate analyses show that some Berber groups (the Tuareg, the Mozabite, and the Chenini-Douiret) are outliers within the NorthAfrican genetic landscape. This outlier position is consistent with an isolation process followed by genetic drift in haplotypefrequencies, and with the high heterogeneity displayed by Berbers compared to Arab samples as shown in the AMOVA. Despite this Berber heterogeneity, no significant differences were found between Berber and Arab samples, suggesting that the Arabization was mainly a cultural process rather than a demographic replacement.
